# std/net.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/net.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

TCP sockets for programs on the hosted target (Linux and
the other targets whose native or C backend links the C library's socket
calls). Built on the `Host` capability, so a kernel or user program that
imports this file is rejected (`E-TARGET`). A call that fails (no such
listener, a closed descriptor, an address in use) gives `Option::None` or
`false`. On Windows the calls go to Winsock, loaded on the first call.

`import "std/net.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

## Functions

### `net_ip4`

```bastio
fn net_ip4(a: u64, b: u64, c: u64, d: u64) -> u64
```

An IPv4 address from its four parts, as `host_net` takes it.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
if lo != 2130706433 { return 1; }
```

### `net_listen`

```bastio
fn net_listen(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Starts listening on `ip`:`port` (port 0 picks a free one).

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_port`

```bastio
fn net_port(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> u64
```

The port a listening socket is bound to.

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    net_close(host, s);
    if p == 0 { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_connect`

```bastio
fn net_connect(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Connects to `ip`:`port`.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1.
match net_connect(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_connect_timeout`

```bastio
fn net_connect_timeout(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64, ms: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Connects to `ip`:`port` within `ms` milliseconds (0 means no limit, as
`net_connect`; more than an hour is cut to an hour). The socket has the
same limit on every later read and write, so `net_recv` gives `None` when
nothing arrives in time and `net_send_all` returns false. The limit is not
applied on Windows yet: there the call blocks as `net_connect` does.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1; the refusal comes at once.
match net_connect_timeout(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1, 2000) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
// A listener that is there: the connection is made and works.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(l) => {
    match net_connect_timeout(host, lo, net_port(host, l), 2000) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, l) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let msg = bfrom("ping");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, msg);
            bfree(msg);
            let mut got = balloc(0);
            match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) {
              Option::Some(n) => { if sent && n == 4 { bad = 0; } },
              Option::None => {},
            }
            bfree(got);
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, l);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_connect6`

```bastio
fn net_connect6(h: &Host, ip: &Bytes, port: u64, ms: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Connects over IPv6 to the 16-byte address `ip` (network order, as
`dns_ip6` makes it) and `port`, giving up after `ms` milliseconds (as
`net_connect_timeout`). `None` if `ip` is not 16 bytes, the host has no
IPv6, or the connection fails.

Example:

```bastio
// An address that nothing answers on port 1 (or a host with no IPv6):
// either way the connection fails.
let lo = bfrom("0123456789abcdef");
let mut bad = 0;
match net_connect6(host, lo, 1, 1000) {
  Option::Some(c) => { net_close(host, c); bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(lo);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_accept`

```bastio
fn net_accept(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Waits for a connection on a listening socket and returns it.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => { bad = 0; net_close(host, a); },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_recv`

```bastio
fn net_recv(h: &Host, sock: u64, max: u64, out: &mut Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Reads up to `max` bytes into `out` (replacing it). `Some(0)` is the end of
the stream.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let msg = bfrom("hello");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, msg);
            bfree(msg);
            let mut got = balloc(0);
            match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) {
              Option::Some(n) => { if sent && n == 5 { bad = 0; } },
              Option::None => {},
            }
            bfree(got);
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_send_all`

```bastio
fn net_send_all(h: &Host, sock: u64, data: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Sends all of `data`, retrying after a partial write. False if the
connection fails first.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
match net_connect(host, lo, 1) {
  Option::Some(c) => { net_close(host, c); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_close`

```bastio
fn net_close(h: &Host, sock: u64)
```

Closes a socket.

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_shutdown_send`

```bastio
fn net_shutdown_send(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> bool
```

Shuts down the sending direction of a connected socket: the peer reads
the end of the stream once it has read what was sent, while this side can
still receive. False if `sock` is not a connected socket, and on the
native backends, which do not have the call yet (the C backend does).

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    match net_connect(host, lo, net_port(host, s)) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let msg = bfrom("bye");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, msg);
            bfree(msg);
            if net_shutdown_send(host, c) {
              // The peer reads the message, then the end of the stream ...
              let mut got = balloc(0);
              let mut n1 = 0;
              let mut n2 = 1;
              match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) { Option::Some(n) => { n1 = n; }, Option::None => {}, }
              match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) { Option::Some(n) => { n2 = n; }, Option::None => {}, }
              // ... and can still answer.
              let ans = bfrom("ok");
              let back = net_send_all(host, a, ans);
              bfree(ans);
              let mut n3 = 0;
              match net_recv(host, c, 16, &mut got) { Option::Some(n) => { n3 = n; }, Option::None => {}, }
              bfree(got);
              if sent && back && n1 == 3 && n2 == 0 && n3 == 2 { bad = 0; }
            } else {
              bad = 0;
            }
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_connect_start`

```bastio
fn net_connect_start(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Starts a connection to `ip`:`port` without waiting for it: the socket
that comes back is non-blocking and the connection is under way. Wait
until the socket can be written to (`host_sys` operation 50, `os_poll`),
then ask `net_connect_result`. `None` when the socket cannot be made, and
on targets without this call (only the Linux C backend has it).

Example:

```bastio
// The socket is made at once, whatever the answer will be; a listener
// that is there accepts the connection.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(l) => {
    match net_connect_start(host, lo, net_port(host, l)) {
      Option::Some(c) => { net_close(host, c); },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, l);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_connect_result`

```bastio
fn net_connect_result(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> u64
```

The outcome of a connection started with `net_connect_start`, once the
socket is writable: 0 when it is connected, else the system's error
number (111, refused, on Linux). 2^64 - 1 if `sock` cannot be asked.
Before the socket is writable the answer is 0 too, so wait first.

Example:

```bastio
// A descriptor that is not a socket cannot be asked.
if net_connect_result(host, 99999) != 18446744073709551615 { return 1; }
```

### `net_listen6`

```bastio
fn net_listen6(h: &Host, ip: &Bytes, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Listens on the IPv6 address `ip` (16 bytes, network order; all zeros is
the wildcard, which also takes IPv4 clients) and `port` (0: any free
port). `None` if `ip` is not 16 bytes, the host has no IPv6, the address
is in use, or the target has no such call (only the Linux C backend has it).

Example:

```bastio
let any = balloc(16);
match net_listen6(host, any, 0) {
  Option::Some(l) => {
    if net_port(host, l) == 0 { bfree(any); return 1; }
    net_close(host, l);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(any);
```

### `net_udp_open`

```bastio
fn net_udp_open(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

A non-blocking UDP socket bound to the IPv4 address `ip` and `port` (0:
any free port; read it with `net_port`). `None` if it cannot be made or
bound, or on targets without UDP (only the Linux C backend has it).

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(u) => {
    if net_port(host, u) == 0 { return 1; }
    net_close(host, u);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_udp_send`

```bastio
fn net_udp_send(h: &Host, sock: u64, ip: u64, port: u64, data: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Sends `data` as one datagram from the UDP socket `sock` to `ip`:`port`.
The count sent, or `None` on failure (no socket, a datagram that is too
large).

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
match net_udp_open(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(a) => {
    match net_udp_open(host, lo, 0) {
      Option::Some(b) => {
        let msg = bfrom("ping");
        let mut bad = 1;
        match net_udp_send(host, a, lo, net_port(host, b), msg) {
          Option::Some(n) => { if n == 4 { bad = 0; } },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        bfree(msg);
        if bad != 0 { net_close(host, b); net_close(host, a); return 1; }
        net_close(host, b);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, a);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_udp_recv`

```bastio
fn net_udp_recv(h: &Host, sock: u64, max: u64, out: &mut Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Receives one datagram of at most `max` bytes (at most 65535) into `out`
(replacing it) without waiting. The answer packs the sender's IPv4 address
(`net_udp_from_ip`), port (`net_udp_from_port`) and the length
(`net_udp_len`); `None` when nothing is waiting or on failure.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
match net_udp_open(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(a) => {
    let mut got = balloc(0);
    match net_udp_recv(host, a, 64, &mut got) {
      Option::Some(p) => { bfree(got); return 1; },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    bfree(got);
    net_close(host, a);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_sockname`

```bastio
fn net_sockname(h: &Host, sock: u64, peer: u64, out: &mut Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

The address of a socket: with `peer` 0 its own (`getsockname`), with 1 the
other end (`getpeername`). The address bytes (4 for IPv4, 16 for IPv6) go
into `out`; the answer is the port in the low 16 bits and 4 or 6 above
them (`net_sockname_port`, `net_sockname_family`). `None` on failure or on
targets without it (only the Linux C backend has it).

Example:

```bastio
let mut a = balloc(0);
match net_sockname(host, 0, 0, &mut a) {
  Option::Some(r) => {},
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(a);
```

### `net_sockname_port`

```bastio
fn net_sockname_port(packed: u64) -> u64
```

The port in an answer of `net_sockname`.

Example:

```bastio
if net_sockname_port(4 * 65536 + 80) != 80 { return 1; }
```

### `net_sockname_family`

```bastio
fn net_sockname_family(packed: u64) -> u64
```

The address family (4 or 6) in an answer of `net_sockname`.

Example:

```bastio
if net_sockname_family(4 * 65536 + 80) != 4 { return 1; }
```

### `net_udp_from_ip`

```bastio
fn net_udp_from_ip(packed: u64) -> u64
```

The sender's IPv4 address in an answer of `net_udp_recv`.

Example:

```bastio
if net_udp_from_ip(72623859711344645) != net_ip4(1, 2, 3, 4) { return 1; }
```

```bastio
fn net_udp_from_port(packed: u64) -> u64
```

The sender's port in an answer of `net_udp_recv`.

Example:

```bastio
if net_udp_from_port(72623859711344645) != 80 { return 1; }
```

### `net_udp_len`

```bastio
fn net_udp_len(packed: u64) -> u64
```

The datagram's length in an answer of `net_udp_recv`.

Example:

```bastio
if net_udp_len(72623859711344645) != 5 { return 1; }
```

### `net_now`

```bastio
fn net_now(h: &Host) -> u64
```

The time in seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, from the system clock (0 if
there is none). The caller of the TLS client gives this as `now`.

Example:

```bastio
// After 2023, and the clock does not run backwards.
let a = net_now(host);
let b = net_now(host);
if a < 1700000000 || b < a { return 1; }
```

### `net_random`

```bastio
fn net_random(h: &Host, n: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == n
```

`n` random bytes (at most 256) from the system's source (`/dev/urandom`,
`RtlGenRandom`, `crypto.getRandomValues`), or `None` when there is none.
The Bytes returned has exactly `n` bytes.

Example:

```bastio
match net_random(host, 32) {
  Option::Some(a) => {
    match net_random(host, 32) {
      Option::Some(b) => {
        // Two draws of 256 bits are the same with probability 2^-256.
        let same = bytes_eq(a, b);
        bfree(b);
        bfree(a);
        if same { return 1; }
      },
      Option::None => { bfree(a); return 1; },
    }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_connect_unix`

```bastio
fn net_connect_unix(h: &Host, path: &Bytes, ms: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Connects to the Unix domain socket at `path` (1 to 107 bytes, no NUL
byte), giving up after `ms` milliseconds (0 means no limit). On Linux a
path that starts with `@` names an abstract socket: the `@` becomes the
NUL byte of the kernel's name (`@/tmp/.X11-unix/X0` is the X server's).
`None` when nothing listens there, the path is too long or the host has no
Unix sockets (Windows, WebAssembly). The socket is read and written with
`net_recv`, `net_send_all` and `net_close` like a TCP one.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("/no/such/socket");
match net_connect_unix(host, p, 1000) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); bfree(p); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(p);
```

### `net_listen_unix`

```bastio
fn net_listen_unix(h: &Host, path: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Listens on the Unix domain socket at `path` (as `net_connect_unix` reads
it); a socket file that is already there makes it fail, so remove it first
with `os_unlink` (an abstract socket leaves none). Accept with `net_accept`.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("/no/such/dir/socket");
match net_listen_unix(host, p) {
  Option::Some(l) => { net_close(host, l); bfree(p); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(p);
```
